en.title: Restore Missing Matrix Values in Global Row Order
en.description: A square matrix with side 4n is divided into n² 4×4 sub-blocks. Each sub-block contains every integer in 1..16 except one, and the missing position is marked -1. First subtract the sum of the numbers present in each sub-block from 136 to get that block's missing value; then sort all missing values in ascending order and fill them into all -1 positions of the original matrix in turn. Positions are ordered row-major (row first, then column) over the whole matrix, not by sub-block order. This site limits 1≤n≤100.
en.input: The first line contains an integer n (1..100), meaning each side has n 4×4 sub-blocks. Then 4n lines follow, each with 4n integers. Each sub-block has exactly one -1, and its other values are 15 distinct integers from 1..16 excluding one value.
en.output: Output the restored matrix of 4n rows, each with 4n integers.
en.explanation: In example 2, the missing positions seen in sub-block order differ from their row-major positions in the whole matrix; so you must first sort the missing values independently, then fill them back in the global row-major order of all -1 positions.
hints: The numbers in each block should sum to 136.
Position order and sub-block enumeration order are two different things.
